# Requirements

Neocortex replaces the Go cortex module with a C++23 engine (cortexd) built as a TigerBeetle-shaped deterministic single-writer state machine over ONE append-only evidence event log per actor. The log is the only ground truth and the only non-rebuildable state: user messages, delivered assistant output, tool calls and results, provider frames, effects, approvals, assertions, intents and open loops all enter as typed events; guidance, doubt and steering have no representable event kind. Everything else — the belief store, entity index, exact SIMD vector lane, BM25, temporal ladder, intent frame and work ledger — is a derived projection rebuildable from the log by replay. Tamper evidence survives as a BLAKE3 MMR with signed checkpoint roots; per-user sealing survives as record AEAD below the hash boundary with the vault KEK to UK to DEK hierarchy and crypto-deletion. Recall becomes deterministic-first: a resident tier, a guaranteed exact-match entity lane, exact brute-force SIMD vector search with recall equal to one, BM25, and recursive temporal descent, composed by one Activate API under a strict non-trimmable tier order. The engine's prime invariant is INV-1 thread continuity: after any crash, respawn, overflow or compaction, the next activation for a conversation deterministically contains the faithful conversation projection, the reconciled work ledger, and the intent frame with the current objective and every open loop. cortexd is a per-user process reached over a Unix domain socket with a versioned FlatBuffers protocol; a Go client package implements the existing resurrection loop interfaces so neo swaps substrates without loop changes. Mechanism lives in C++, policy in Go: cortexd never calls a model or the network. The hello-world sessionjournal design is absorbed — its typed event taxonomy and exact provider-byte sidecar are promoted into the log — so Matrix ships one event-sourcing system, not two. Migration is an export: a Go tool walks the existing Pebble store and replays it through the import gate; old and new run side by side behind the memory seam until the regression corpus is green and the owner approves cutover.

## Requirement 1: The evidence log: one append-only, sealed, tamper-evident ground truth

**User Story:** As the Matrix memory substrate, I want every fact about what happened to enter one typed append-only log, so that nothing Neo experienced can be lost, forged, or double-recorded.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE engine SHALL persist one append-only event log per actor as fixed-format frames (length, crc32c, lsn, kind, wall timestamp, actor, conversation, sealed FlatBuffers payload) in bounded segment files, with group-commit durability barriers.
2. THE event kind taxonomy SHALL be exactly the set frozen in agent.lock.kvx (conversation, work, intent, memory, and control kinds, including exact provider-byte frames absorbed from sessionjournal). Guidance, doubt, steering, and rejected answers SHALL have no representable kind.
3. ON boot, THE engine SHALL verify the log tail by checksum, truncate at most one torn frame at the physical tail, and refuse to start on any interior corruption, reporting the exact lsn.
4. A BLAKE3 merkle mountain range over frame hashes SHALL provide tamper evidence with O(log n) range proofs; checkpoint roots SHALL be ed25519-signed and verifiable offline, preserving the MEMORY VERIFIED property.
5. EVERY frame payload SHALL be sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305 record AEAD below the hash boundary under the vault KEK to UK to DEK hierarchy, with associated data binding actor, lsn, and kind; key destruction SHALL render the actor's log unreadable (crypto-deletion).
6. WRITE-AHEAD ordering SHALL hold for work: a tool_call event SHALL be durable before the tool executes, and only a delivered_msg event SHALL represent user-visible assistant output.

## Requirement 2: Deterministic single-writer state machine with rebuildable projections

**User Story:** As the engine, I want all mutable state to be a pure function of the log prefix, so that rebuild is always correct, testing is exhaustive, and replication is possible later.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ONE writer thread SHALL apply events in lsn order; the core SHALL obtain time, entropy, and I/O exclusively through injected interfaces so that identical logs produce byte-identical projections.
2. ALL projections (belief store, entity index, vector lane, BM25, temporal ladder, intent frame, work ledger, conversation heads) SHALL live in per-actor LMDB environments keyed with their applied-lsn checkpoint, and deleting any or all projections followed by replay SHALL reproduce them byte-identically.
3. READERS SHALL serve queries from consistent snapshots without blocking the writer, via epoch-pinned read transactions.
4. A deterministic simulation harness SHALL drive the engine with simulated clock, I/O faults (torn writes, short reads, reordered or lying fsync), and process kill at arbitrary lsns, asserting replay convergence and recovery invariants; it SHALL run in CI at every wave.
5. THE engine SHALL enforce a static memory budget: large allocations at startup, per-request arena allocators reset per operation, and a hard bound on peak resident memory per actor.

## Requirement 3: Belief store behind one write gate with mandatory provenance

**User Story:** As Neo's durable memory, I want beliefs to exist only as gated projections of evidence, so that duplicates, poisoning, and evidence-free convictions are structurally impossible.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. BELIEFS (typed facts, preferences, constraints, goals, identity records) SHALL be created and revised exclusively by the apply-time write gate from assertion and consolidation events; no API SHALL write a belief directly.
2. EVERY belief SHALL carry provenance lsn ranges into the log; the schema SHALL make a provenance-free belief unrepresentable.
3. THE gate SHALL perform canonical-identity typed upsert with supersession chains and bi-temporal validity (as_of queries over both valid time and transaction time).
4. WHEN an incoming belief contradicts a live head with a different canonical identity, THE gate SHALL record a typed conflict edge that the activation composer is obligated to surface whenever either side surfaces.
5. A negative-existence assertion (a claim that a thing is gone, defunct, or nonexistent) SHALL be rejected by the gate unless its provenance includes corroborating tool_result evidence.
6. EXPLICIT remembers (MCP remember verbs, memory_mutate, preference feedback, profile writes) SHALL enter as assertion events through the same gate; user-directed retraction SHALL be a typed retract event honored by projections and recall.

## Requirement 4: Deterministic-first index plane

**User Story:** As recall, I want existence to be guaranteed and relevance to be enriched, so that a stored identifier can never fail to surface (the Moltbook class dies structurally).

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AN entity index SHALL deterministically extract operational identifiers (domains, URLs, paths, hex and structured ids, proper names) from every applied event and belief into an exact-match table; WHEN an identifier or its entity appears in an activation query or turn text, its records SHALL surface with guaranteed recall.
2. THE vector lane SHALL be exact brute-force SIMD scan over quantized (int8, with binary prefilter) mmap-resident vectors — recall equal to one, deterministically; no approximate-nearest-neighbor structure SHALL be built.
3. EMBEDDINGS SHALL arrive from clients as embedding events bound to a target lsn or belief; records without embeddings SHALL remain fully reachable through the entity and lexical lanes; vector state SHALL rebuild from the log alone.
4. A BM25 lexical index over roaring bitmaps SHALL cover messages and beliefs; ranked fusion across semantic and lexical lanes SHALL use reciprocal rank fusion with a deterministic tiebreak.
5. A temporal ladder projection SHALL maintain wall-clock windowed rollups over the log with recursive descent handles, so coarse-to-exact time navigation (the RLM pattern) survives the rewrite.

## Requirement 5: INV-1: thread continuity is never lost

**User Story:** As Neo, I can never lose track of the current conversation, the work done in the active thread, and what I need to do next — across any crash, respawn, overflow, or compaction.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE activation for a conversation SHALL always contain: a faithful projection of every exchanged turn (coarsened but never dropped), the work ledger with every effect's reconciled status, and the intent frame (current objective plus every open loop). All three SHALL be composed deterministically, never probabilistically.
2. INTENT SHALL be write-ahead: intent_set events SHALL be durable before dependent work dispatches; loop_opened events SHALL create obligations that appear in every subsequent activation until a loop_closed event with a typed reason (done, abandoned with cause, handed_off, superseded) exists. Nothing SHALL close silently.
3. THE work ledger SHALL distinguish dispatched, committed, returned, and outcome-unknown effects from the log alone; boot after a crash SHALL mark in-flight effects for reconciliation before the thread continues.
4. SUCCESSOR briefing SHALL be evidence replay: the respawn path SHALL consume the window projection, work ledger, and intent frame, and SHALL NOT consume any predecessor-written narrative summary as authority.
5. THE activation budget SHALL trim in the fixed order: enrichment lanes first, mid-conversation coarsening second, and SHALL never trim the resident tier, the intent frame, or the work ledger tail; an intent frame alone exceeding budget SHALL surface as an engine invariant violation, not a trim.
6. THE simulation harness SHALL kill the engine at every lsn of a scripted multi-turn multi-tool conversation, boot a successor, and assert ac_1 through ac_4 hold on the very next composed activation; this property SHALL run in CI.

## Requirement 6: One activation composer

**User Story:** As the agent loop, I want one composed, budgeted context bundle per iteration, so that five uncoordinated retrieval systems collapse into a single deterministic contract.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ONE Activate operation (conversation, query, budget) SHALL replace the legacy Activate, Retrieve, LexicalConversation, episodic, and conversational-recaller lanes, composing in strict tier order: resident (identity, hard constraints, active goals), intent frame, work ledger tail, conversation projection, entity-lane hits, conflict-obligated beliefs, fused semantic plus lexical enrichment, and temporal descent handles.
2. THE composer SHALL be a pure read: identical log prefix, query, and budget SHALL yield a byte-identical bundle, pinned by golden vectors.
3. BUDGETING SHALL use a caller-supplied token model (a counting callback or table), not a bytes-per-token heuristic; each tier SHALL report its spend and what was trimmed.
4. THE bundle SHALL be structured (typed sections with URIs and provenance), leaving rendering to the client; every surfaced item SHALL be attributable back to log lsns or belief ids.
5. SURFACED-memory attestation (used or ignored signals) SHALL return as events so salience learning remains possible as a projection concern, not an engine hot-path concern.

## Requirement 7: cortexd process, local protocol, and the Go client seam

**User Story:** As the Matrix runtime, I want one brain process per user reached over a local socket, so that every consumer shares one consistent memory and a cortex crash never kills the agent.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. CORTEXD SHALL run as one process per user, serving a Unix domain socket with a versioned, FlatBuffers-framed request/response and subscription protocol; it SHALL make no outbound network connections and SHALL never invoke a model.
2. PER-connection capability tokens SHALL scope each client to an actor namespace; neo, the executor daemon's cortex routes, and MCP tooling SHALL all be clients of the same process rather than co-owners of store files.
3. A Go client package SHALL implement the existing resurrection loop interfaces (ActivationSource, TurnRecorder, EvidenceJournal, Consolidator sink, CheckpointStore) over the protocol, so the runtime loop swaps substrates without loop code changes.
4. A cortexd crash SHALL never take down the agent process: the client SHALL degrade gracefully (bounded queue then honest failure), the supervisor SHALL restart cortexd, and reconnection SHALL resume with no lost acknowledged writes and no duplicate application of unacknowledged writes (idempotent append keyed by client sequence).
5. TURN checkpoints (the turnstate role) SHALL be servable from checkpoint events and a latest-checkpoint projection, so mid-turn cursor recovery and thread continuity are one mechanism.
6. AN admin surface (same socket, separate capability) SHALL expose health, per-operation latency histograms, log/projection stats, verification status, and a manual rebuild trigger.

## Requirement 8: Robustness regime: toolchain, safety discipline, and adversarial CI

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the engine held to a database-kernel bar, so that memory safety and crash correctness are proven properties, not C++ hopes.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE engine SHALL build as C++23 with the exact pinned toolchain, flags, and hardened standard library recorded in agent.lock.kvx; the core SHALL compile with exceptions disabled and use typed std::expected errors on all fallible paths.
2. OWNERSHIP discipline SHALL hold: no raw owning pointers or naked new/delete, arena allocation per request, bounded queues everywhere, and clang-tidy enforcement of the ruleset in CI at zero warnings.
3. CI SHALL run address, undefined-behavior, and thread sanitizer matrices over the full test suite, libFuzzer targets over every decoder (frame parser, FlatBuffers verification, protocol framing, query input), and property-based tests for upsert idempotency, replay convergence, MMR consistency, and AEAD round-trips.
4. THE dependency set SHALL be exactly the vendored, digest-pinned list in agent.lock.kvx; the build SHALL be reproducible and cross-compiled for amd64 and arm64 with a static runtime.
5. EVERY untrusted input boundary (socket frames, imported events, on-disk state) SHALL be verified before trust; a malformed input SHALL produce a typed rejection, never undefined behavior, proven by fuzz corpora kept in-tree.

## Requirement 9: Hard Neo cutover, absorption, and structural Cortex-v1 exclusion

**User Story:** As the owner, I want Neo to know only Neocortex, so Cortex-v1 cannot influence, fail, or silently recover any Neo turn.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. NO Neo source file, test, module dependency, build target, configuration key, command-line flag, or runtime construction path SHALL import, name as a selectable substrate, open, query, write, proxy, or fall back to centra/core/cortex. A structural CI gate SHALL prove the exclusion.
2. NEOCORTEX SHALL be Neo's sole memory engine with no substrate selector. Startup SHALL require a valid Neocortex client configuration; an unavailable or unhealthy cortexd SHALL produce an honest typed failure and SHALL never route to Cortex v1.
3. THE hello-world sessionjournal lane SHALL be absorbed: its event kinds and exact provider-byte sidecar are promoted into the log taxonomy, and no second event-sourcing system SHALL remain on the cutover path.
4. EXTERNAL consumers (executor daemon cortex routes, bridge, MCP tooling) SHALL be re-pointed to cortexd clients; the MCL compile-cache seed SHALL derive from the neocortex checkpoint root by an owner-approved rule.
5. CORTEX v1 MAY remain temporarily for unrelated consumers, but it SHALL be outside Neo's source and module graph and unreachable from the Neo process. Deletion or migration of unrelated consumers remains separately owner-gated.
